clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 0-671 of the held text jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8504-exemption-james-e-amos-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt): signed August 7, 1940. The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), exempts James E. Amos from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending January 31, 1942. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. First end: the order's own stated end, January 31, 1942 (operative sentence: "for a period of one year ending January 31, 1942."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of January 31, 1942); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when January 31, 1942 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held. Later event, not an end: Executive Order 8917, signed October 16, 1941, further exempts the same person; its recital names this order ("by Executive Order No. 8504 of August 7, 1940") and its operative sentence runs "ending January 31, 1943". Like this order it has no effective-date wording, so I read it as effective on signing. MOMMSEN-I rechecked this stated end against both held witnesses. Cited EO 8917 APP uses section/sec. in the authority reference where GPO uses Section/Section; same 715a reference and grant. Capitalization/abbreviation only.
